title: Mrs. Magdalen Lloyd, Netherlands Subject. Dauxion De Ruffe

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE

11 / 7 / 33）

July 11 33.

SECRET

Dear Barton,

I have to inform you that Mrs. Magdalen Lloyd
is at present on a visit to Shanghai endeavouring to
find customers for the curio business which she is
conducting in Peking.

Mrs. Magdalen Lloyd was born a subject of the
Netherlands, but has acquired British nationality by
marriage. She arrived in Shanghai from Hongkong on
October 10, 1929. She secured employment shortly after-
wards as manageress of the "Lotus d'Or", a curio shop at
No. 593/5 Avenue Joffre, which was owned by Mr. d'Anxian
de Ruffe, a well known French lawyer. Her husband,
Mr. C.G. Lloyd, was at that time employed here by Elm
& Co. Ltd, but they did not live together.

On November 12, 1929, Mrs. Lloyd instituted
divorce proceedings in H.B.M. Supreme Court at Shanghai
and was granted a Decree Nisi on January 24, 1930.

Mrs. Lloyd resigned from the "Lotus d'Or" in the
Autumn of 1930 and left Shanghai for Peking where, it is
said, she established a business of her own. It is said
that Mrs. Lloyd's resignation from the "Lotus d'Or"
resulted from dissatisfaction on the part of Mr. d'Anxian
de Ruffe with the way she managed the business during
a period that he was absent in Europe.

Yours sincerely,

J. Barton, Esq.,
British Consulate-General,

1933年7月11日。

机密

亲爱的巴顿：

兹通知您，玛格达伦·劳埃德夫人（Mrs. Magdalen Lloyd）目前正访问上海，试图为其在北平经营的古玩生意寻找客户。

玛格达伦·劳埃德夫人生为荷兰臣民，但通过婚姻取得了英国国籍。她于1929年10月10日从香港抵达上海。不久后，她受雇担任“金莲”（Lotus d'Or）古玩店的经理，该店位于霞飞路593/5号，由著名法国律师德·鲁菲先生（Mr. d'Anxian de Ruffe）所有。她的丈夫 C.G. 劳埃德先生当时受雇于本地的 Elm & Co. Ltd 公司，但两人并未同居。

1929年11月12日，劳埃德夫人在上海英国陛下最高法院提起离婚诉讼，并于1930年1月24日获得临时离婚判决（Decree Nisi）。

劳埃德夫人于1930年秋季从“金莲”辞职，离开上海前往北平，据说她在那里自立门户经商。据称，劳埃德夫人从“金莲”辞职的原因是，德·安西安·德·鲁菲先生（Mr. d'Anxian de Ruffe）对其在欧洲期间管理业务的方式感到不满。

此致
敬礼，

J. 巴顿 先生，
英国驻上海总领事馆，

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, JULY 7, 1933

Mrs. Magdalen Lloyd of Peking
recently received an invitation to
go to the United States to help in
the organisation of a new Oriental
Art Museum in New England. One
of the well known American art
collectors asked Mrs. Lloyd to com-
plete his Chinese collection for the
new museum which he intends to
establish in his native city near
Boston. Mrs. Lloyd left Peking
for Shanghai on July 2 to make
arrangements for her American
trip in the autumn.

The Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
Shanghai.

Dear Sir, confidential
I beg to acknowledge the receipt of your letter dated
the 5th instant, giving me information about Mrs. Magdalen Lloyd,
and thank you very much for all the trouble you have taken.
I am relieved to know that the Municipal Police know nothing
against her character, as the Administrative Commission has
granted her permission to open a curio store in the Diplomatic
Quarter.

With renewed thanks,
Yours faithfully,

W. P. Thomas
Secretary.

Dear Sir,

With reference to your letter dated April 14,
1932, I have to state that Mrs. Magdalen Lloyd was
born a subject of the Netherlands, but has acquired
British nationality by marriage. She arrived in
Shanghai from Hongkong on October 10, 1929. She secured
employment shortly afterwards as manageress of the
"Lotus d'Or", a curio shop at No. 593/5 Avenue Joffre,
which was owned by Mr. d'Auxion de Ruffe, a well known
French lawyer. Her husband, Mr. C.G. Lloyd, was at that
time employed here by Elm & Co. Ltd, but they did not
live together.

On November 12, 1929, Mrs. Lloyd instituted
divorce proceedings in H.B.M. Supreme Court at Shanghai
and was granted a Decree Nisi on January 24, 1930.

Mrs. Lloyd resigned from the "Lotus d'Or" in
the Autumn of 1930 and left Shanghai for Peking where,
it is said, she established a business of her own. It
is said that Mrs. Lloyd's resignation from the "Lotus
d'Or" resulted from dissatisfaction on the part of Mr.
d'Auxion de Ruffe with the way she managed the business
during a period that he was absent in Europe.

During her stay in Shanghai, Mrs. Lloyd lived
at various addresses, including the Plaza Hotel and
No. 597 Avenue Joffre.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT

（印：File No... SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. B. REGISTRY SECTION 2 Station, N.. D 3336 Date May 2, 19 32 Date 2 / 5 / 32.）

Subject (in full) Letter from Secretary of Administrative Commission of Legation
Quarter, Peking, re: Mrs Magdalen Lloyd.

Made by D.S.Prokofiev Forwarded by （签名）

With reference to the letter of April 14, 1932 from
the Secretary of the Administrative Commission of the Legation
Quarter, Peking, on the subject of Mrs Magdalen Lloyd, enquiries
show that this lady is Dutch by birth and British by marriage.
She has been married twice and has a son by first husband.
On October 10, 1929 she arrived in Shanghai from
Hongkong, together with her son, and took up residence at the Plaza
Hotel. Shortly afterwards she secured employment as manageress of
the " Lotus d'Or ", a curio shop at No 593-5 Avenue Joffre, owned
by Mr. d'Auxion de Ruffé, a well known local French lawyer. On Oc-
tober 22, 1929 she removed from the Plaza Hotel to No 597 Avenue
Joffre. Her husband, Mr. C.G.Lloyd, who was at that time employed
with the Elm & Co., Ld, resided apart from his wife.
On November 12, 1929 Mrs Lloyd instituted divorce pro-
ceedings in H.B.M. Supreme Court at Shanghai. The petition which
charged her husband with adultery, was heard on January 24, 1930
when she was granted a Decree Nisi which was made absolute on Ju-
ly 26, 1930.
During the autumn of 1930 she resigned from her po-
sition at the " Lotus d'Or " owing, it is rumoured, to the fact
that Mr. d'Auxion de Ruffé was dissatisfied with the manner in
which the business had been conducted during his absence to Europe.
Some time later she proceeded to Peking with the
object of establishing her own business.
We have been unable to confirm the information that
she was ever employed with the "Gray Trading Company" in Shanghai,
but it is quite possible that she had business dealings with this
firm.
Apart from the foregoing nothing is known in this of.

（左侧边缘手写批注：17 June D.）

主题（全称） 北平使馆界行政委员会秘书关于玛格达伦·劳埃德夫人的来信。

由 D.S. 普罗科菲耶夫（Prokofiev） 制作 由 （签名） 转发

关于1932年4月14日北平使馆界行政委员会秘书就玛格达伦·劳埃德夫人一事所致的来信，经查询显示，该女士出生时为荷兰人，婚后为英国人。她结过两次婚，并与第一任丈夫育有一子。
1929年10月10日，她与儿子一同从香港抵达上海，入住华懋饭店。不久后，她受雇担任“金莲”古玩店的经理，该店位于霞飞路593-5号，由当地著名法国律师德·奥克西翁·德·鲁菲先生（Mr. d'Auxion de Ruffé）所有。1929年10月22日，她从华懋饭店搬至霞飞路597号。她的丈夫 C.G. 劳埃德先生当时受雇于 Elm & Co., Ld 公司，与妻子分居。
1929年11月12日，劳埃德夫人在上海英国陛下最高法院提起离婚诉讼。指控其丈夫通奸的诉状于1930年1月24日开庭审理，当时她获得了临时离婚判决，该判决于1930年7月26日生效成为绝对判决。
1930年秋季，她辞去了在“金莲”的职务，据传闻，原因是德·奥克西翁·德·鲁菲先生对其在欧洲缺席期间经营业务的方式感到不满。
一段时间后，她前往北平，目的是建立自己的生意。
我们未能证实她曾在上海的“灰色贸易公司”（Gray Trading Company）受雇的信息，但她完全有可能与该商行有过业务往来。
除上述情况外，本局对此事一无所知。

（左侧边缘手写批注：6月17日 D.）

LA COMMISSION ADMINISTRATIVE
DU
QUARTIER DIPLOMATIQUE.
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
PEKIN. April 14th S. 1932 REGISTRY.
No. D 3536.
Date 20 / 4 / 32.

The Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
International Settlement,
Shanghai.

Dear Sir,

I venture to enquire if you could give me any confidential information regarding a certain Mrs. Magdalen Lloyd. This lady, who is, I am told, Dutch by birth and British by marriage to a British husband, now divorced, has been in Peking for about two years and has a curio business in the Grand Hotel de Pekin, and she has applied to the Commission for permission to open a curio show-room in the Diplomatic Quarter. I am told that previously she was in Shanghai, in the employ of a firm called I think "the Great Trading Company" dealing in ladies silk underwear, etc.,. I have also heard that she was there connected in some way with a gentleman named Auxion de Buffe, or some such name. I would like to find out what was her reputation while she lived in Shanghai, and why she left her employment there.

I shall be grateful for any information you can give me.

Thanking you in anticipation,

Yours faithfully,

W. P. Thomas
Secretary.

上海。

尊敬的先生：

冒昧询问，您能否提供关于某位玛格达伦·劳埃德夫人的任何机密信息。据悉，这位女士出生时为荷兰人，后与一位英国丈夫结婚并取得英国国籍，现已离婚。她在北平已居住约两年，并在北京饭店经营古玩生意，且已向本委员会申请许可在外交区开设一间古玩陈列室。据闻，她此前曾在上海受雇于一家我想名为“大贸易公司”（the Great Trading Company）的商行，经营女士丝绸内衣等商品。我还听说她在那里以某种方式与一位名为奥克西翁·德·布菲（Auxion de Buffe）或类似名字的绅士有关联。我希望了解她在上海居住期间的声誉如何，以及她为何辞去那里的工作。

如您能提供任何信息，我将不胜感激。

预先致谢，

此致
敬礼，

W. P. 托马斯
秘书。
